newsitem.title: USA: Home Savings revises year results down.
newsitem.headline: Home Savings revises year results down.

text.p: Home Savings Bank of Siler City Inc Monday said it has revised it results for the year ended September 30, 1996, with net income now at $120,000 for the year as opposed to the previously announced $515,739.

The revision was due to two nonrecurring special items, the firm said. One item previously announced was the expense of the SAIF special assessment affecting all savings banks and certain other financial institutions. Home Savings Bank previously announced that its special assessment share to recapitalize the SAIF fund amounted to $253,568.

The Bank's net earnings were also hurt by the accounting treatment for retirement of debt of the ESOP loan. The ESOP retired a significant amount of its debt as a result of the special one time dividend of $4.80 per share paid to all shareholders in August 1996.
This repayment of the loan caused a large number of the shares in the ESOP to be released and allocated to the individual employees, the company said.

Such allocation and release became a major compensation expense item which was required to be recognized by September 30, 1996. Assuming an increase in the per share price, the large allocation caused by the dividend will result in a smaller future impact on compensation expense, they said.
